newsitem.title: USA: Simpson lawyers to seek mistrial over lie detector.
newsitem.headline: Simpson lawyers to seek mistrial over lie detector.

text.p: Lawyers for O.J. Simpson said at his civil trial on Tuesday they would seek a mistrial because the jury was told he failed a lie detector test after the murder of his ex-wife and her friend.
Attorney Robert Baker told Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki he was preparing a motion seeking a mistrial on the grounds the jury should have been told to disregard such polygraph evidence.

Simpson said during questioning on Nov. 25 that he had refused to take a police polygraph test the day after the murders but he went to an independent expert the next day and was hooked up to a polygraph machine. But he specified he believed it was just a demonstration.

He was asked about the test by a plaintiffs' lawyer, Daniel Petrocelli, who said during the questioning that Simpson had scored a minus 22 on the test, which he said indicated "extreme deception." The information came from a book by author Lawrence Schiller in which he quoted sources in Simpson's criminal trial as saying the ex-football star had taken the so-called lie detector test.

Simpson was acquitted in criminal court in October last year of murdering his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman in June 1994. He is being sued in civil court by the victims' families, who are seeking damages.

Baker, arguing that polygraph evidence was inadmissible in criminal trials under California law, told the judge he would seek a mistrial. "We are preparing a motion. I suggest the court mistry the case and unfortunately start all over again."
Baker said he had stated in his opening statement that second-hand information from Schiller's book "American Tragedy: The Uncensored Story of the Simpson Defence" should be disregarded by the jury.
But Fujisaki told the attorney: "Mr Baker, you slipped it in and Mr Petrocelli took advantage of it." The judge adjourned the trial to review his instructions to the jury.
